candidate.title: Ancient West African foragers in the context of African population history
candidate.authors: Lipson M., Ribot I., Mallick S., Rohland N., Olalde I., et al., Reich D.
candidate.ask_addressed: Africa: what do linguistics, ancient DNA and archaeology show about the Bantu expansion (dates, routes, Lipson et al. 2020, Patin et al. 2017, Bostoen's work) and what is disputed?
candidate.quote: implying that these individuals are not representative of the primary source population(s) ancestral to present-day Bantu speakers
candidate.summary: Genome-wide data from four children buried c. 8000 and 3000 years ago at Shum Laka (Cameroon), in the probable Bantu homeland, show ancestry close to West-Central African hunter-gatherers, unlike most Niger-Congo speakers today. The authors say the results neither support nor contradict a central role for the Grassfields in Bantu origins.
candidate.limits: Four individuals from one site; it does not date or route the Bantu expansion, and does not show who the Bantu source population was. It frames the Bantu spread as c. 3000-1500 BP on the strength of cited linguistic and archaeological work, not its own data.

reason: strand_unsupported: the quoted passage says Shum Laka individuals are unrepresentative of Bantu source populations; it states no transfer of language or ancestry, and the strand's -1000/500 span and 'inferred' directness rest on background citations, not the quote

candidate.authors: Socrates Scholasticus (trans. in NPNF series 2, vol. 2)
candidate.ask_addressed: Aksum's adoption of Christianity (Ezana inscriptions; Rufinus)
candidate.quote: Rufinus assures us that he heard these facts from Edesius, who was afterwards ordained to the priesthood at Tyre
candidate.summary: Socrates tells how Meropius's youthful kinsmen, Edesius and Frumentius, were seized, served the Indian king, and Frumentius asked Athanasius at Alexandria for a bishop, then returned as bishop. He names Rufinus as having had the story from Edesius.
candidate.limits: I could not open Rufinus's own Ecclesiastical History (10.9-10), only a later retelling that names it as source. 'Indians' here is the interior India of the text, taken by scholars to be Aksum (Rukuni 2021); Socrates writes a century after the events.

text.edition: NPNF series 2, as hosted by New Advent

composition.basis: Wikipedia 'Socrates of Constantinople' (opened) gives his life as c. 380 to after 439; no composition date was read on an opened page

text.witness: Not established from the page opened

strand.what: Christian worship and a bishop for Aksum through Frumentius

reason: strand_unsupported: the quoted sentence only says Rufinus heard the Frumentius story from Edesius; it does not name Aksum or say Christianity was carried there (Aksum is the researcher's reading of 'India', not in the quote)
